The statement balances acknowledgment of resilient real activity with a clearly restrictive policy stance. Holding the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50% and continuing balance-sheet runoff (caps of $60B Treasuries and $35B agency MBS) is consistent with Taylor-type prescriptions when inflation is above target and labor markets are tight (Taylor; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler). Emphasis on “cumulative tightening” and “lags” mirrors the monetary transmission literature in which higher policy rates and tighter credit conditions work through loans and spending with delays (Bernanke–Mihov; interest-rate-to-loans channel). Reaffirming a firm 2% objective and willingness to adjust policy helps contain Barro–Gordon inflation bias by bolstering credibility and anchoring expectations. Operationally, reliance on administered rates and standing facilities (IORB, ON RRP, repo) reflects the post-2008 floor/corridor framework for precise rate control, consistent with modern central banking practice and lender-of-last-resort principles adapted to abundant reserves. Net tone: cautious and anti-inflationary despite solid growth—supportive for long-run price stability but restrained for near-term risk assets.
